item.title: Coming This Thursday | AmiciMusic: The Sound of America — Mon Nov 9 — Asheville Art Museum
item.description:
Thursday, November 12, 2026 | 7:00 pm – 9:00 pm | $22 for Members; $25 for non-members; $12 for students Event Details and Tickets AmiciMusic returns with a thrilling program entitled “THE SOUND of AMERICA.” Pianist and Artistic Director Daniel Weiser will be joined by violinist Tim Schwarz from Philadelphia in this exciting exploration of the incredible diversity of our American sound.
The program includes Spirituals and Ragtime as well as Blues-inspired works by W.C. Handy and William Grant Still, the Native-American inspirations of Charles Cadman, the Jewish influence on Ernest Bloch, the country fiddling in Aaron Copland, and the Latin rhythms in Bernstein’s West Side Story.
Weiser and Schwarz served as the 1996 U.S. Artistic Ambassadors of Music for which they performed over 50 concerts in 11 countries in the Middle East and Southeast Asia showcasing our American music

item.title: Warren Wilson Berea Baptist Church Hike — Mon Nov 9, 9:00 AM
item.description:
Asheville Mountains-to-Sea Trail Hiking Club 2.0 We'll meet at 9:00 a.m. on Riceville Road, across from Berea Baptist church and plan to leave no later than 9:10 a.m.
We'll hike in the woods along the Bull Creek Trail and over to the Swannanoa River trail and back. This is a gently undulating hike through serene woods and along peaceful waterways. We hike at about 3.2 mph.
Then length of this trail is 5-6 miles, depending upon how far we hike along the river; and we will return to the cars by 11:00 to 11:15. Well behaved dogs on leashes are welcome.
Mountains-to-Sea-Trail hikes are designed for fitness and community among people who are already reasonably fit. It's not an endurance hike by any means, but it is designed so we can get our hearts beating a bit while still being able to have a conversation and meet new people. The typical pace for a hike of this sort is 3.0 to 3.2 mph.

item.title: The Body of the Golem: A Life in Portraiture — Sun Nov 15, 2:00 PM
item.description:
Artist and writer Riva Lehrer brings together portraiture, Jewish tradition, disability, and the figure of the golem for the 2026 Phyllis Freed Sollod Memorial Lecture in the Mountain View Room of the Sherrill Center. Through art and storytelling, Lehrer explores who gets labeled “monstrous,” who has the power to define that label, and what becomes possible when people claim their own bodies and identities. This lecture is sponsored by the Center for Jewish Studies. The event is free and open to the public. Accessibility UNC Asheville is committed to providing universal access to all of our events. If you have any questions about access or would like to request reasonable accommodations that will facilitate your full participation in the film screenings, please contact Stephanie Bullick, Director of Accessibility, at accessibility@unca.edu. item.title: Mountains-to-Sea Trail Highway 25 toward Bent Creek — Mon Nov 23, 9:00 AM
item.description:
Asheville Mountains-to-Sea Trail Hiking Club 2.0 This is a fairly easy hike, and we go at a high average to low advanced speed, which is roughly about 3.0 to 3.2 mph. There are no super long hills. It's pretty undulating all the way.
Well behaved dogs on leashes are welcome to attend.
When you arrive, park at the gravel lot across from the trail head. You'll see some people gathering by their cars. I've recently corrected the PIN setting on the map, so it should be correct. Here are some directions to use too: When going south on Hendersonville Road, go past Carolina Day School and turn right at the Blue Ridge Parkway exit. When you get to the parkway turn RIGHT. You will see parking on the left and right side of the road. Park there.

item.description:

item.title: 12/6 St. Nick Day Walk in Waynesville from Mast General to Middle School & Back — Sun Dec 6, 2:00 PM
item.description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group It's time for childlike wonder. Let's do a St. Nicholas Day walk in Waynesville and see the Christmas decorations.
Meet at 2:00 in front of Mast General Store, 63 N. Main St., Waynesville NC 28786. We will meet at the rocking chairs in front of the door to the shoe department.
The walk goes past public art, to Frog Level for a brief stop at Panacea Coffee Company, to Waynesville Middle School, through an interesting neighborhood, and back to the start point.
There are some hills, so some may want a walking pole (I will take 2); sneakers should be fine. Dogs are welcome. Strollers should be ok. Bring plenty of water and a protein snack. Dress appropriately for the weather. Consider a hat and, even though it is December, sunscreen.
Parking is easier a block to either side of Main Street. Mast General Store doesn't have a public restroom, but we can direct you to one nearby should you need it. There are one or two restrooms along the route.
Source:

item.title: Collectors' Circle | Acquisition Dinner — Mon Dec 7, 5:00 PM — NC
item.description:
Join us, Collectors’ Circle Members, as the time has come for our end-of-year celebration! After a year of social and educational gatherings, the year-end acquisition dinner is the Circle’s biggest event. Collectors’ Circle Members are invited to the Museum for an evening of delicious food and artistic stewardship. Annual purchases to grow the Museum’s Collection is made possible by the Collectors’ Circle yearly dues, creating the Museum’s acquisition fund. The 2026 acquisition dinner features exciting catering by Céline & Company. RSVP by Email Pending space available, Collectors’ Circle Members are welcome to invite guests to the acquisition dinner for $100 each. If your guests have been invited with interest in joining this specialized group, please contact our Membership Associate, Annabeth Hannaford, at ahannaford@ashevilleart.org or 828-253-3227 x117. For more information and a look at previous acquisitions, visit our Collectors’ Circle page. RSVP by Email
Source: Ashevill
